comparator.name: Fiscale Economie
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official UvA curriculum and 2026-2027 study guide, checked 2026-09-29, define a complete 180-EC pathway with three 60-EC years and no formal route. Year 1 builds economics, business, accounting, finance, quantitative and qualitative research foundations and introduces fiscal economics. Year 2 combines general and business taxation with property and company law, public finance, accounting, fiscal methodology, tax technology and payroll taxation. Year 3 adds a bound elective, tax procedure, corporate income tax, VAT, European and international tax, director-major-shareholder taxation, advanced finance, taxable-profit calculation, a graduation seminar and a 6-EC bachelor thesis. The marketing-page table omits Belastingheffing en Technologie and Loonheffingen and shows two year-3 entries without credits; the official 2026-2027 study guide supplies both omitted 3-EC year-2 courses and confirms Fiscale Winstberekening and Bachelorscriptie Fiscale Economie as 6 EC each. The resulting components total exactly 180 EC.
components: One approved bound elective; the official study guide lists six current 6-EC options.
Compulsory independent bachelor thesis in fiscal economics.

candidates.label: Tax policy, behaviour and social equity

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the programme's fiscal-economics identity, economic effects of taxation, public budgets, tax-system comparison and economics-law combination. Two further generator-backed directions remain. Business taxation and the effects of tax rules on firms and international structures support an accounting, finance and commercial-regulation route. Employment, household effects, policy design, ethics and fair taxation support a behavioural and social-equity route. Each direction is coherent and feasible at UCR while remaining explicit about the absence of specialist Dutch tax teaching. The closest match differs from each related direction by six courses; the two related directions differ by eleven. Both additional candidates are included, reaching the maximum of three alternatives.

alternatives.label: Economics, taxation & public finance
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines the strongest available UCR economics and public-finance sequence with business, accounting, finance, law, EU institutions and research methods. The label states those available fields and does not imply that UCR offers a specialist fiscal-economics degree.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response combines economics, taxation and public-spending analysis with accounting, finance, business and legal foundations, EU and international institutions, empirical research and persuasive communication.
progression: Law, Society & Justice in semester 1 precedes every later course that formally requires it. Research Methods & Statistics precedes all selected economics courses with that prerequisite, while Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations precedes Transnational Business Law, International Business & Governance and Money, Banking & Finance. Introductory economics precedes the advanced economics sequence conceptually. The Art of Rhetorical Communication precedes Rhetoric in Action. The final year concentrates advanced private law, EU politics, governance, econometrics, finance and qualitative research. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternatives.label: Business taxation, accounting & finance
alternatives.labelReason: This direction concentrates the available UCR business, accounting, finance, commercial-law, governance and quantitative courses around the fiscal consequences of company decisions. The label does not claim specialist instruction in Dutch corporate taxation.
alternatives.concept: A business-focused response combining economics, accounting, finance, commercial regulation, international business, strategy, organisational behaviour and empirical research to examine how fiscal rules shape firms and investment decisions.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route removes criminal law, constitutional and administrative law, EU law, EU politics, international-relations theory and qualitative social research. It adds digital business strategy, organisational leadership, business and regulation in the age of AI, behavioural economics, market research and applied rhetoric. Six of the 24 courses differ, and the organising choice shifts from a broad law-and-public-finance comparison to business organisation, commercial decision-making and finance.
progression: Law, Society & Justice, Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations and Introduction to Economics establish the legal, business and economic strands in semester 1. Research Methods & Statistics precedes all selected courses that formally require it; Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations precedes Strategy & Digital Transformation, Transnational Business Law, International Business & Governance, Money, Banking & Finance and Market Research. The Art of Rhetorical Communication precedes Persuasive Communication. The final year advances from accounting, macroeconomics and organisational leadership to private law, global governance, finance, econometrics, behavioural economics and independent market research. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternatives.label: Tax policy, behaviour & social equity
alternatives.labelReason: This direction uses UCR public economics, behavioural economics, law, politics and sociology to examine tax design, labour and household effects, ethics and fairness. The label signals a policy and social-analysis route, not a specialist tax qualification.
alternatives.concept: A public-policy and social-science response combining taxation and redistribution analysis with behavioural economics, law, political institutions, sociology, ethics and mixed research methods to study fair and effective tax systems.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route removes the business-foundations, accounting, international-business, macroeconomics, finance and transnational-business-law courses. It adds sociology, modern and contemporary social theory, political philosophy, peace and conflict, and behavioural economics. Six of the 24 courses differ from the closest match and eleven differ from the business direction. The route is therefore organised around public authority, institutions and society rather than commercial practice.
progression: Law, Society & Justice, Introduction to Economics and Introduction to Sociology establish the legal, economic and social foundations in semester 1. Law, Society & Justice precedes every later law course with that formal prerequisite, and Research Methods & Statistics precedes all selected advanced economics courses. International law, constitutional law and international-relations theory precede the advanced EU-law, EU-politics and conflict courses conceptually. Introductory rhetoric precedes Rhetoric in Action, and introductory sociology precedes advanced contemporary social theory conceptually. The final semester brings together qualitative methodology, econometrics, behavioural economics and applied public communication. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

blocks: Both orient students to the interaction of law, institutions and economic activity; UCR provides a broader legal-social foundation.
Both establish core microeconomic and macroeconomic concepts for analysing economic activity.
Both introduce organisations and business decision-making; UCR does so through entrepreneurship and business planning.
Both introduce financial accounting and the interpretation of business financial information.
Both develop microeconomic analysis of markets, incentives, efficiency and behaviour.
Both develop macroeconomic analysis; UCR places it in an international policy context.
Both use quantitative methods for empirical economic analysis; UCR provides advanced econometric application.
Both develop finance and investment analysis; UCR combines banking, risk and financial decision-making.
Both teach qualitative research design, data collection, interpretation and reporting.
UCR has no dedicated orientation course introducing fiscal economics as a professional and academic field.
Both directly examine taxation, government finance, public spending, redistribution, efficiency and equity.
Both address property and private-law relationships relevant to economic and fiscal arrangements; UCR is comparative and non-jurisdiction-specific.
Both work within the European legal order; UCR covers EU law broadly rather than specialist European tax doctrine.
Both address international legal structures; UCR provides public-international-law foundations rather than specialist international tax law.
UCR has no dedicated course in Dutch general taxation.
UCR has no dedicated introduction to Dutch business taxation.
UCR has no specialist payroll-tax course.
UCR has no specialist Dutch tax-procedure course.
UCR has no specialist corporate-income-tax course.
UCR has no specialist value-added-tax course.
UCR has no specialist course on taxation of directors and major shareholders.
UCR has no specialist taxable-profit-calculation course.
Both examine legal rules governing companies and business relationships; UCR concentrates on transnational commercial law rather than Dutch reporting law.
Both examine how technology changes business and regulatory practice; UCR treats this across the economy rather than as tax technology.
UCR Accounting & Corporate Finance provides one accounting course but no second dedicated financial-accounting course.
UCR has no dedicated management-accounting course.
UCR has no third specialist financial-accounting course.
UCR Money, Banking & Finance is already aligned to the first finance component; there is no second dedicated finance course.
Behavioural Economics is an eligible coherent UCR emphasis for examining how policy and framing affect economic choice; the comparator permits one bound elective.
Both develop methodological judgment; UCR concentrates on research design and statistics rather than fiscal-economic philosophy of science.
Both require students to design, conduct, analyse and communicate an independent research project; UCR uses a business-research setting.
Both develop structured argument and effective presentation of complex academic work; UCR focuses on rhetoric rather than a fiscal graduation seminar.

notes.text: The Amsterdam programme is a specialist fiscal-economics degree combining a continuous sequence in Dutch taxation with economics, accounting, finance, property and company law, tax technology, European and international tax, fiscal methodology and a fiscal-economic thesis. UCR can combine public economics and taxation analysis with business, accounting, finance, broad law, politics, sociology and research methods. It does not teach the Dutch tax code, tax procedure, payroll tax, VAT, corporate taxation or the programme's multi-course accounting sequence. These pathways therefore compare related economic, business, legal and policy fields; none reproduces the external fiscal-economics discipline or its professional preparation.
